security.note: No new ir.model.access or ir.rule records; the one new entity (stock_notification_product_partner_rel M2M between product.product and res.partner) and all extension fields reuse the ACLs/record-rules of website_sale, sale_stock and stock. Public storefront access is governed by website_sale's existing ecommerce_access gate; controller writes use sudo().

views.note: No standalone view records; ~390 XML LOC inherit-extend website_sale/stock views in place (product.template form adds the Sell-when-Out-of-Stock / Show-availability / threshold / out-of-stock-message fields; res.config.settings adds the website defaults + website_warehouse_id; stock.picking list adds website_id; website_sale_stock_templates.xml injects the product_availability QWeb block into the product page). Storefront UX is QWeb + frontend JS, not backend views.

behavioral_notes.observation: Two routes. (1) /shop/add/stock_notification (jsonrpc, public, website=True) is the back-in-stock subscription endpoint: it email_re-validates the address, resolves/creates a partner via mail.thread._partner_find_from_emails_single, and if product._has_stock_notification(partner) is False appends it to product.product.stock_notification_partner_ids (sudo M2M stock_notification_product_partner_rel); for the public user it also stashes the product id and email in request.session so the page can show the 'subscribed' state. (2) WebsiteSaleStockVariantController overrides /website_sale/get_combination_info with a bare @route() that does request.update_context(website_sale_stock_get_quantity=True) before super() -- this context flag is the gate that makes product.template._get_additionnal_combination_info emit the live stock payload (free_qty/cart_qty/show_availability/out_of_stock_message) every time the product page recomputes a variant/qty. Side-effects invisible in metadata.

product.template adds four storefront-availability config fields: allow_out_of_stock_order (Boolean, default True -- 'Sell when Out-of-Stock'), show_availability (Boolean, default False), available_threshold (Float, default 5.0 -- the qty below which the remaining count is shown), and out_of_stock_message (Html, translatable). _get_additionnal_combination_info (only when context website_sale_stock_get_quantity is set and product is storable) exposes on-hand to the page: it reads website._get_product_available_qty(product) which is product.with_context(warehouse_id=website.warehouse_id.id).free_qty, floor-rounds it (rounding_method='DOWN', precision_digits=0) into res['free_qty'], and -- only when allow_out_of_stock_order is False -- also returns res['cart_qty'] = cart._get_cart_qty(product). It is free_qty (forecast on-hand minus reservations for the website warehouse), NOT virtual_available, that the storefront displays; virtual_available is not used here. _get_additional_configurator_data adds the same free_qty (as product._get_max_quantity) for the modal product configurator. Pure read side-effect, not in metadata.

THE CART CLAMP. website_sale's add/update routes call the hook sale.order._verify_updated_quantity(order_line, product_id, new_qty, uom_id) (parent default returns (new_qty, '') -- i.e. no clamp). This override, for a storable product whose allow_out_of_stock_order is False, computes (product_qty_in_cart, available_qty) via _get_cart_and_free_qty -> _get_free_qty = product.with_context(warehouse_id=self._get_shop_warehouse_id()).free_qty (the website warehouse, or all warehouses if none set), floor-rounds available_qty, and if available_qty < total_cart_qty returns allowed_line_qty = available_qty - (other-lines cart qty) instead of the requested qty -- so the line is capped to free_qty and the cart can never exceed on-hand. It attaches a sale.order.line.shop_warning ('You ask for X but only Y is available', or a 'not added'/'cart updated' message) for the storefront. When allow_out_of_stock_order is True the override defers to super() and no clamp is applied. Side-effect (silent qty downgrade + warning) invisible in metadata.

Out-of-stock gating is centred on product.product._is_sold_out(): a product is never sold out if not is_storable or allow_out_of_stock_order, else sold-out iff website._get_product_available_qty(self) <= 0. It drives: _website_show_quick_add (hide Add-to-Cart on grids), the product_availability QWeb (free_qty<=0 -> show out_of_stock_message or 'Out of Stock' badge + 'Get notified when back in stock' form; free_qty<=available_threshold -> warning badge 'N <uom> in stock' with '(n in your cart)'), product.ribbon assign='out_of_stock' (_is_applicable_for shows the ribbon when sold out), product.feed._prepare_gmc_stock_info (forces GMC availability 'out_of_stock'), and product.product._to_markup_data (schema.org InStock/OutOfStock on the page). The order-confirmation side-effect: sale.order._check_cart_is_ready_to_be_paid (called at checkout/payment) runs sale.order.line._check_availability for every line and raises ValidationError joining all shop_warnings if any line's cart_qty exceeds its free_qty -- blocking payment of a cart that drifted out of stock between add and pay. product.product._send_availability_email (the back-in-stock cron) renders website_sale_stock.availability_email_body, mails each subscribed partner via mail.mail, and removes them from stock_notification_partner_ids. All side-effects, not in metadata.

it_architecture.application: website_sale_stock (eCommerce real-time availability extension; bridges website_sale <-> stock)
software_services: /website_sale/get_combination_info (jsonrpc, public: product-page availability/qty recompute, overridden to inject stock payload)
logical_data_erm: website -> stock.warehouse (warehouse_id: the shop's source warehouse for availability)
information_flows: read (stock -> storefront): website._get_product_available_qty(product) = product.with_context(warehouse_id=website.warehouse_id.id).free_qty -> product.template._get_additionnal_combination_info -> product page free_qty/cart_qty/availability message
guard (cart): sale.order._verify_updated_quantity clamps the added line to free_qty - cart_qty when allow_out_of_stock_order is False (no over-ordering vs on-hand)
guard (confirmation): sale.order._check_cart_is_ready_to_be_paid -> sale.order.line._check_availability raises ValidationError (blocks payment if cart drifted out of stock)
notify (out-of-stock -> back-in-stock): /shop/add/stock_notification subscribes res.partner; ir.cron _send_availability_email mails subscribers when _is_sold_out becomes False, then clears the M2M
auto_install: true -> activates whenever website_sale, sale_stock and stock_delivery are all present
frontend_components: WebsiteSale.prototype (patch: stock-notification handlers + post-add availability refresh)

capabilities: Real-Time eCommerce Stock Availability Display (on-hand / free_qty on product page & grid)
Out-of-Stock Sales Policy (block vs continue selling, per-product and website-default)
Cart Over-Order Prevention (clamp line qty to available on-hand)
value_streams: Browse-to-Order (availability leg): shopper sees live free_qty -> add-to-cart clamped to on-hand -> checkout availability re-check gates payment -> confirmed order feeds the sale_stock delivery chain
Out-of-stock -> back-in-stock re-engagement: sold-out product -> shopper subscribes -> replenishment -> notification email -> return to /shop
policies: allow_out_of_stock_order (per product.template; website default default_allow_out_of_stock_order) governs whether out-of-stock products can still be ordered
available_threshold + show_availability govern when/whether the remaining quantity is shown
automation: _verify_updated_quantity clamps cart qty; _check_cart_is_ready_to_be_paid blocks checkout on shortage; ir.cron _send_availability_email sends back-in-stock mails
website.warehouse_id selects which warehouse's free_qty is the source of truth (else all warehouses)
stakeholders: eCommerce / Website Manager (sets availability policy & threshold)
metrics: free_qty / available on-hand surfaced per product (storefront availability indicator)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_sale_stock is an availability extension of the website_sale storefront, so it inherits website_sale's value-configuration: a value NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad) -- the online shop mediates between many anonymous/portal visitors and the catalog over shared channel infrastructure. This module enriches that channel with real-time inventory signalling (free_qty on the product page, low-stock thresholds, out-of-stock badges/ribbons, back-in-stock subscriptions) and with demand-side guard-rails (clamping cart quantity to on-hand and blocking checkout on shortage). Its primary economic activity is therefore selling over the web with accurate availability, i.e. APQC 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services (3.0=Market and Sell), matching website_sale. It is classified primary (revenue/customer-facing sell-side channel feature), not support: it directly shapes what the shopper can buy. A secondary facet touches APQC 4.x Deliver (4.x=Deliver Physical Products): the availability number it reads is stock free_qty for the website warehouse and a confirmed cart still flows into the sale_stock delivery chain (delivery orders, stock.picking.website_id) -- but website_sale_stock itself only reads stock to gate selling and does not perform fulfilment, so 3.0 is primary and 4.x is only a touchpoint via its sale_stock/stock_delivery dependencies.

standard_capabilities: Live product-page availability (free_qty for the website warehouse) with optional 'N in stock' display
Per-product 'Sell when Out-of-Stock' toggle + website-wide default (res.config.settings)
Configurable low-stock display threshold (available_threshold) and translatable out-of-stock message
Cart quantity automatically capped to available on-hand; shop_warning shown to shopper
Checkout/payment blocked when a cart line is no longer available
Out-of-stock ribbon (product.ribbon assign='out_of_stock') and schema.org / Google Merchant availability
Back-in-stock email subscription + cron notification when replenished
Website-level source warehouse selection for availability checks
typical_fits: B2C shop that hides/blocks out-of-stock products and shows remaining quantity near zero
Single-warehouse storefront reading free_qty from the website warehouse
Continue-selling (backorder) products that ignore stock while still displaying status
Back-in-stock waitlist capturing latent demand for sold-out variants
common_gaps: Multi-warehouse / per-location availability beyond the single website warehouse (handled by website_sale_collect, out of scope here)
Reservation/allocation of cart stock (cart qty is checked, not reserved, until order confirmation)
Pre-order / dated-availability / drop-ship lead-time messaging on the storefront
Bespoke availability rules (e.g. show ATP/virtual_available instead of free_qty, or supplier stock)

curl jsonrpc http://localhost:8069/shop/add/stock_notification {product_id, email}  # subscribe to back-in-stock (auth=public)

open_questions: Exact reservation semantics: cart qty is checked against free_qty at add and at checkout but not reserved in stock, so two concurrent carts can both pass _verify_updated_quantity for the same units -- final arbitration happens only at order confirmation / procurement (sale_stock).
How website_sale_collect / pickup overrides _get_shop_warehouse_id and _get_free_qty to consider the chosen delivery warehouse rather than website.warehouse_id.
Whether free_qty (on-hand minus outgoing reservations) vs virtual_available is always the right ATP signal for backorder/MTO products, since the storefront deliberately reads free_qty only.
